Strategic Foresight Leaders

SFL is a conference series for people trying to make sustainability work inside a real business. They come for the conversation they cannot have in their own office: what worked, what cost too much, what they would do differently. The brand had to own that room.

Where it started

Everything in this category looks the same. Bright green, rising arrows, a planet held in two hands.

None of that sounds like the people who actually turn up, who tend to be more pragmatic than hopeful.

The event01

The roomcomes first.

Almost everyone meets SFL in a hall, in front of a screen the width of the stage. That first minute decides what people think the whole thing is worth, so the screens carry one line at full height and let nothing compete with it.

The idea02

The momentbefore it starts.

The lights go down, one line appears on the screen, and the room knows something large is about to start. That moment became the mark, the palette and the way every screen is lit.

The mark03

Two bars anda gap.

Two bars at different heights with a half disc of light between them. The gap between the bars is the horizon. I kept the sun floating above the line for a while and it always read as a dot that had come loose, so it sits on the line instead.

SFL Photography

On photographyIt goes in the darkest part of the frame, never on a horizon the picture already has. Two horizons in one image is one too many.

When it gets smallUnder about 16 px the sun stops being a shape and turns into a smudge, so it drops out and the bars carry the mark alone.

On paperThe sun turns moss. Lime belongs on screens, where it behaves like light. Printed, it just looks like a highlighter.

Colour05

Mostly dark,with one light.

Five greens, from almost black to bone. The accent lives between yellow and green and gets used sparingly, somewhere under three percent of a layout. Spread it wider and it stops meaning anything, which is more or less what happened to green in this whole category.

Type06

Everything in Geist,except the name.

Geist does everything that has to be read, from a headline on a stage screen to a time on a badge. Archivo Expanded shows up only inside the logo, so the name always arrives in the same voice.

In use07

Where it hadto hold up.

A brand like this gets judged in two places: a room with the lights down, and somebody’s hand. It has to be the most expensive looking thing on the street and still survive a laser printer.

Session cards, programme

Moodboard08

Low light,long view.

Late sun, deep shadow, and scale that makes a person small in the frame. People appear mid conversation rather than looking at the camera. Anything you can touch is glass, uncoated paper or cloth. The images here are AI generated and stand in for a shoot.

Voice09

A room of people who decide what gets built.

Short linesOne idea per line. If it needs a comma to survive, make it two lines.

No urgencyNo countdowns, no last chance. Confidence does the work that urgency does for everyone else.

ConcreteName the industry, the decision, the year. Vague optimism is what everyone else is already doing.

What will still hold in ten years?
